marks.gloss_en: לא תלבש שעטנז is juxtaposed to גדילים תעשה לך: in the place of the mitzva of tzitzit, the kilayim prohibition yields -- an aseh overrides a lav
a positive command overrides a plain negative command (the accepted rule)
all the needed teachings (two-cord/four-cord shiur, tokhef, shua-tavui-venuz) issue from שעטנז alone, so the freed words stay free
as circumcision (an aseh) overrides Shabbat (a karet-lav), so any aseh overrides a karet-lav
מה למילה שכן נכרתו עליה שלוש עשרה בריתות -- circumcision is uniquely weighty
as the Paschal offering overrides Shabbat, so any aseh overrides a karet-lav
מה לפסח שכן כרת -- its own neglect incurs karet, so it is an unusually strong aseh
as the daily offering overrides Shabbat, so any aseh overrides a karet-lav
מה לתמיד שכן תדיר -- it is constant, so it is an unusually strong aseh
from circumcision and Pesach together, by their common denominator
their common denominator is itself a stringency: neglect of either incurs karet
from Pesach and the daily offering together, by their common denominator
שכן צורך גבוה -- both are requirements of the altar, not personal obligations
from circumcision and the daily offering together, by their common denominator
שכן ישנו לפני הדיבור -- both preceded the giving of the Torah; NB this pircha holds only aliba of the view that the desert olah was the tamid, a qualification the schema cannot record
from all three together, by their common denominator
ומכולהו נמי שכן ישנן לפני הדיבור -- all three preceded the giving of the Torah
a positive command overrides a plain negative command (the accepted rule, presupposed at 5b.6)
honoring parents does not override Shabbat -- כולכם חייבין בכבודי
the baraita speaks of שחוט לי בשל לי -- karet-level labour; so absent the verse, the aseh WOULD have overridden a karet-lav
the override of even a karet-level prohibition could be derived from honoring parents -- which is why עליה had to be written
